text: No open hi-hat. It answers notes 36, 38 and 42 only, so the open-hat hits AI Producer writes on note 46 are silent. Heard as missing off-beat hats in the house and techno drum clips.
At default settings a 0.5 input comes out at 0.96, almost double. A limiter that adds level by default is not safe to drop on a master, so it was left out of the mix.
At default settings a 0.5 input peaks at 1.12, more than double. Loading it on a playing track would cause a jump in level.
No output level control. A separate SimpleGain was needed just to set its level in the mix.
No output level control, and the default patch has its filter nearly closed (cutoff at 10% of range). A SimpleGain was needed to set its level.
The default patch has a slow attack with chorus and reverb on, which does not work for bass. Five settings had to be changed by hand. A few starting patches (bass, pad, lead) would save that.

Live lists 49 AudioForge plugins but 61 are installed. Shakuhachi, Sitar and Classic Monosynth are among those missing from Live's browser. Six appear as 'AudioForge - Name' while the rest use the plain name.

The frozen sound holds about 13 dB below the level that was playing (RMS 0.08 against 0.35). With Phase Random above zero the phases come from the live input, not the frozen frame, which is the likely cause.
Its tone and level were chosen from the code's comments and preset names when the silence bug was fixed. Nobody has listened to it yet.
It recommends Operator, Analog and Wavetable, which Live Intro does not have, and cannot load instruments itself. It writes notes with a call Live has deprecated since version 11.
Nothing in AudioForge does what Live's Utility did in the mix: gain, stereo width and mono in one device. SimpleGain and PanUtil each cover part of it.

There is no AudioForge drum machine with a full house or techno kit (kick, snare, clap, closed and open hat). DrumSynth has three sounds; AnalogKick, SnareSynth, HiHat and TomSynth each need their own track.
